Ex-Gov. Pataki, who put Regents in place, rips ‘incredibly stupid’ axing of tests: ‘Really sad day for New York’

"It seems like the Education Department’s main function right now is to disguise the fact that too many New York State schools are failing to educate our kids.''

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Gov. Kathy Hochul and her Dem cronies are dunces for allowing the dumbing down of the state’s high-school-diploma requirements by ditching the Regents exams, says the ex-gov who helped put the tests in place.

“Getting rid of the Regents is incredibly stupid,” said George Pataki, the Republican three-term New York governor from 1995 through 2006, to The Post.

“It seems like the Education Department’s main function right now is to disguise the fact that too many New York State schools are failing to educate our kids,” Pataki said.

“So instead of doing the appropriate testing so that corrective measures could be taken to improve [performance], they simply get rid of the tests to hide their failure.”

“This is really a sad day for New York.”

Pataki was slamming the state’s education policy-making board and Education Department for phasing out the exams by 2028 that are currently required to earn a high school diploma.

There are no alternative graduation requirements in place, at least yet.

The Regents exams that students have needed to pass in math, English, science and Global Studies to obtain a diploma became a graduation requirement during Pataki’s tenure and under then-state Education Commissioner Richard Mills.

The Board of Regents earlier this month voted to make them optional as they work to develop alternative graduation requirements.

Pataki also referenced the Brooklyn elementary school that controversial woke New York Times writer Nikole Hannah-Jones highlighted in a recent piece she wrote. Hannah-Jones admitted in the report that she knowingly “sacrificed” her daughter by sending her to the badly failing school, where her child did not thrive, to make a point to try to get other black parents to keep their kids at the neighborhood school.

“This is a disgrace,” Pataki said.

“The next time Democrats talk about income inequality, ask them how their subservience to the teachers union is helping low income minority kids get a step up in life,” he said.

Current 12th graders will be the last graduating class required to pass at least four Regents exams in math, English, science and Global Studies.

Students on track to graduate in 2028 will no longer be required to pass the exams to finish high school, but they can still take them.

The graduation policy is set by the 17-member New York Board of Regents, whose members are appointed by Democrats who control the legislature.

The governor does not have a direct role in appointing the Regents. But the Democratic Hochul has enormous power over school funding and has passed laws impacting education.

Now the debate over scrapping the Regents exams is becoming a hot potato in the race for governor.

Hochul, seeking re-election to a second term, is facing off against Republican Bruce Blakeman, the current Nassau County executive.

“We pay the highest taxes in the nation under Kathy Hochul, yet too many of our children are still not getting the results they deserve,” Blakeman said in a statement. “Taxpayers and students deserve higher standards, stronger schools and real accountability for the enormous amount of money New York spends on education.

The Board of Regents and Education Commissioner Betty Rosa have debated replacing the state exams for years after appointing a blue-ribbon panel in 2019 to exam alternative graduation requirements.

Hochul addressed the explosive issue for the first time only last week, expressing concerns about the switch as she’s about to face voters again.

“Governor Hochul shares the concerns many New Yorkers have raised about the decision to eliminate the current standards for earning a high school diploma and the lack of clarity about what will replace them,” a Hochul rep said Sunday.
